title: edge-evidence-aggregation-and-approval-timelines-prd
summary: Sketch for a lightweight evidence aggregation model, approval timeline SLAs, and operator-facing runbook for private deployments where customers manage parts of the network. Goal: provide forensically useful snapshots without bloated retention costs and with predictable approval latency for customer-facing changes.
body:
Context

This doc captures an early PRD-level proposal for two tightly coupled capabilities in Private: (1) lightweight evidence aggregation (compact forensic snapshots) for customer-managed networking and operator actions, and (2) explicit approval timeline SLOs and graceful rollback tokens for changes that cross guarded boundaries. We frequently get asks from security-conscious customers: keep an auditable trail, but don’t force multi-GB logs into our long-term store. Also operators want a clear, short UI path to validate and approve changes with bounded latency.

Problem statement

- Customer-managed networking (VPC handoffs, peering, on-prem edge) means some evidence lives outside our control. When we do capture artifacts, teams struggle to: (a) compress evidence into a compact, queryable form; (b) attach approval provenance to the change; (c) offer predictable approval timelines for SLAs.
- Current proposals either keep everything (costly) or sample too aggressively (insufficient for post-incident forensics).

Goals

1) Define a compact evidence model that preserves minimal-forensic fidelity for key events (change intent, config diff, operator assertion, customer consent capsule).
2) Define approval timeline SLAs and a configurable grace/auto-approve window for customer tiers (enterprise vs self-serve).
3) Deliver operator UX and a short oncall runbook for triage and rollback using a lightweight rollback token mechanism.
4) Keep cost predictable: define retention tiers and a cost model per change bundle.

Non-goals

- This is not a full replacement for SIEM forwarding (we still expect customers to forward raw telemetry to their SIEM).
- We are not building long-term immutable cold storage here; this is for 30–180 day forensic windows.

Design overview (high level)

1) Compact Evidence Bundle (CEB)
- What: a single compressed JSON-LD-like artifact capturing: change metadata (who/when/which-run), signed operator assertion (OID), compact config diff (delta), customer-provided consent token (if applicable), short traces (2–5 spans), and an evidence checksum.
- Why: bundles are small (typically <200KB) but contain the minimal items needed for forensic reconstruction and legal audit requests.
- How: we run a pre-commit serializer in the control plane that extracts the delta and canonicalizes it; store signed CEB in the evidence index.

2) Retention tiers & indexing
- Hot (7 days): full CEB retained and searchable with fast query.
- Warm (30 days): CEBs retained, full-text index limited to headers and diff tokens.
- Cold (configurable up to 180d): only manifest + checksum and a link to export/escrow.
- Export/escrow: for customers with regulatory needs, automated export to customer S3/KMS on approval.

3) Approval timeline model
- For any change that touches a guarded path (VPC handoff, public egress rule, key rotation) we attach an Approval Policy: {tier, SLO_seconds, grace_window_seconds, fallback_behavior}.
- Example presets:
  - Enterprise managed: SLO 2h, grace 30m, fallback: block + manual owner escalation.
  - Dedicated self-serve: SLO 30m, grace 5m, fallback: auto-revert to previous config.
  - Emergency: SLO immediate, but must include post-facto CEB and operator justification.
- The control plane enforces deadlines; if not approved by SLO+grace, we route to fallback policy.

4) Operator UX and the compact approve panel
- Panel shows: change summary (1–2 lines), impacted resources, CEB checksum, suggested rollback token, links to diffs, and a single-click approve/deny with optional comment.
- Quick actions: escalate (opens pre-populated Slack channel), attach evidence to Jira/GH issue, request customer attestation.

5) Rollback tokens and short-lived attestations
- When an approval completes, the system mints a rollback token (signed, TTL-limited) that operator can use to initiate an automated rollback path without further approval.
- Tokens recorded in CEB and audit index. Tokens are single-use.

Operator runbook (rough)

- On alert: check Approvals dashboard -> filter by SLA-breaches -> open CEB -> validate checksum and operator assertion.
- If change was unauthorized: use rollback token (if available) -> trigger revert pipeline -> update CEB with revert result.
- If evidence ambiguous: export CEB to forensic export (S3) and open an incident with customer contacts.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics

- 95% of guarded changes have a CEB <250KB.
- Approval SLOs met in 90% of cases for enterprise preset over a 30-day rolling window.
- Post-incident forensics: mean time to produce full evidence export to customer <15 min for hot-tier artifacts.
- Cost: average monthly evidence storage increase <2% for customers on Dedicated plans.

Security/privacy considerations

- All CEBs encrypted at rest with customer KMS for private deployments (option).
- Evidence exports must be signed and have tamper-evident checksums.
- Sensitive values (secrets, keys) omitted or redacted by default — we capture references not secret material.

Open questions / TODOs

- How small can canonicalized diffs be for common firewall/VPC changes? (Action: engineering benchmarking spike).
- Legal: do regulators in APAC require longer default retention? (Action: legal consult).
- UX: should rollback tokens be scoped to operator role or change id? (Action: security/infra decision).
- Exports: define S3 export contract and retry semantics for intermittent network.

Notes to self

- Need prototype serializer lib in python + node to test bundle sizes across sample change corpus from ENG-logs.
- Coordinate with SRE for emergency fallback automation (runbook snippets to commit to runbooks repo).

Appendix: short example CEB outline (pseudo)

- change_id: CHG-2025-0007
- initiator: operator@customer.com
- timestamp: 2025-02-03T14:22:11Z
- diff_summary: ["remove egress 0.0.0.0/0 from sg-abc123", "add route to 10.0.20.0/24 via bng-2"]
- operator_assertion: signed-pkcs7
- customer_consent_token: optional-signed-jwt
- traces: minimal-span-list (2 spans)
- checksum: sha256:abc...

--end of draft--

This is still a working draft; want to get engineering spike estimates and legal input before circulating to customers. Comments welcome — especially from SRE and legal on retention floor and from engineering on serializer cost.
